items.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: I mean I was a James Brown fan you know and stuff like that.

ctx.x: Yeah. It’s interesting, it’s like just when the audience, at least some of them, would catch up with them, he’d be on to something else.

On to something else. A lot of people didn’t like “Bitches Brew.” The real kind of like young crowd — that turned the corner crowd — the Jimi Hendrix people, you know, really liked that album. Because it was, again for want of a better word, psychedelic. The beats were different and the music was soulful and the young folks really liked that. Because that period of time, Jimi Hendrix and this huge musical revolution, with Donovan and all of these people, who by the way I would listen to too. I mean I was a James…
At that session, was there anything on paper musically or was it pretty much—
